message.content:
Based on my search, here are the main ways to pay federal taxes online:

## 1. IRS Direct Pay (Free)
- **Website:** https://www.irs.gov/payments/direct-pay-with-bank-account
- **Cost:** Free
- **How it works:** Pay directly from your checking or savings account. No registration required, but you'll need to verify your identity using information from a prior-year tax return (address, Social Security number, date of birth, and filing status).
- **Features:** Schedule payments up to 365 days in advance, modify or cancel payments up to two business days before processing, receive email notifications.
- **Availability:** Monday-Saturday: midnight to 11:45 p.m. EST; Sunday: 7 a.m. to 11:45 p.m. EST

## 2. Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) (Free)
- **Website:** https://www.eftps.gov
- **Cost:** Free
- **How it works:** A secure system from the U.S. Treasury for both individuals and businesses. Requires enrollment and you'll receive a PIN by mail.
- **Features:** Schedule payments up to a year in advance, comprehensive payment history for up to 16 months, available 24/7 online or by phone (800-555-4477).
- **Note:** EFTPS no longer accepts new users as of 2025; existing users are being transitioned to IRS accounts or Direct Pay.

## 3. IRS Online Account
- Access through https://www.irs.gov
- Manage and make payments through your personal IRS account

## 4. Debit/Credit Card or Digital Wallet (Fees Apply)
- **Processors:** Pay1040 or ACI Payments
- **Debit card fee:** ~$2.10-$2.15 per payment
- **Credit card fee:** 1.75%-1.85% of payment (minimum $2.50)
- **Digital wallets accepted:** Venmo, PayPal, Click to Pay, and others
- **How it works:** Go to the processor's website, enter payment amount and card information

## 5. Electronic Funds Withdrawal (EFW) (Free)
- Available when e-filing through tax software or with a tax preparer
- Authorize direct debit from your bank account as part of the filing process

## 6. IRS2Go Mobile App (Free App, Possible Fees)
- Download on iOS or Android
- Make payments via mobile version of IRS Direct Pay (free) or with debit/credit card (fees apply)

## Important Update (March 2025 Executive Order)
A new executive order requires electronic payment of federal taxes. Paper checks and money orders will no longer be accepted after **September 30, 2025**. This affects:
- Q4 2025 estimated tax payment (due January 15, 2026)
- All future tax payments

Exceptions apply for individuals without banking access, emergency situations, or other legal exemptions.

---

Sources:
1. https://fiscal.treasury.gov/payments-to-government/electronic-federal-tax-payment-system-eftps
2. https://www.nerdwallet.com/taxes/learn/pay-irs-options
3. https://www.zinnerco.com/zinner-blog/executive-order-requires-electronic-payment-of-federal-tax
4. https://www.taxact.com/support/1142/2020/eftps-online-electronic-federal-tax-payment-system
5. https://www.hrblock.com/tax-payment-center/
6. https://www.tax1099.com/irs/irs-federal-tax-payment/
7. https://www.wallstreetmojo.com/electronic-federal-tax-payment-system/
8. https://www.aggarwalcpa.com/blog/the-electronic-federal-tax-payment-system
